summary: SLA governance audit and cleanup for support-tooling rulebook
description:
Issue summary: Internal support tooling contains diverging SLA template names and duplicated routing rules introduced during the Dec 2025 rule-engine migration. This has caused inconsistent SLA enforcement across internal queues (some P1 tickets are not being escalated to SRE on 30m schedule).

Impact: Partial enforcement of P1/P2 SLAs for internal support channels; potential missed wake-up pages for on-call SREs. Affected teams: Internal Support (triage), SRE runbooks that depend on canonical SLA labels, and the automation that generates SLA reports. No customer-facing incidents reported yet but internal SLAs are the source of several PagerDuty misses in the last three weeks.

Environment: support-tooling (prod), routing-engine v2, rulebook index: /opt/support/rules/v2 (internal).

Steps to reproduce:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOOLING_API" https://tooling.internal.redwood/api/v1/sla_templates | grep -i P1
2) Compare template names returned against routing rule config: /etc/support/routing_rules.yaml
3) Run the reporting job (support-sla-reporter) for the last 14 days and observe tickets that should have triggered P1 escalation but show no escalation action.

Observed behavior: There are at least three templates that appear semantically identical but have different slugs (e.g. "P1-30m", "P1-30m_v1", "p1-30-min"). Routing rules sometimes point at older slugs. The SLA reporter aggregates by slug, so metrics are split and alert thresholds are not being hit.

Logs / dashboards:
- Support tooling audit log: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/abcd-support-tooling/sla-audit?orgId=1
- Reporter job run: https://ci.internal.redwood/builds/6543 (last failed run referencing missing template)

Initial hypothesis: Migration created duplicate template entries; the rule-engine accepted both old and new slugs without normalization. Downstream reporter was not updated to canonicalize slugs, fragmenting metrics and preventing escalations.

Proposed short-term mitigation: Add one-off reconciliation that maps legacy slugs to canonical slugs and backfills missing escalations for the last 7 days. Medium-term: enforce schema validation in the rule-engine CI and add a pre-deploy lint that rejects new/duplicate SLA slugs.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-11: Pulled template list from tooling API; found 47 SLA templates, 6 appear to be duplicates by human-readable description.
2026-02-12: Cross-referenced routing_rules.yaml; 4 rules reference legacy slugs that are not present in canonical mapping table.
2026-02-13: Re-ran support-sla-reporter locally with normalization flag; metrics aggregated correctly when normalization applied.
2026-02-15: Confirmed reporter failure in CI due to nil-pointer when template slug missing (see CI build 6543).
